messages:
jia: heads-up — noticed console charts getting slower for a subset of users after last canary. FCP/TTFP spikes, and some large chunk downloads (~6MB each) happening repeatedly :thinking_face:

sam: saw the same in RUM. Lots of 200s but with `cache-control: no-cache` on chunk responses, so SW/network ends up revalidating all the time. Potentiially explains re-download loops.

ben: deploy-bot shows the canary rolled at 10:42 UTC and then the global rollout started at 10:53. Could be a routing change in the rollout policy. deploy-bot: deploy/console-20260301-frontend -> canary -> gradual

alex: quick dump from edge logs:
```
GET /static/chunks/charting~bundle.abcdef.js 200 - cache-control: no-cache, pragma: no-cache
GET /static/chunks/charting~bundle.abcdef.js 200 - age: 0, via: 1.1 cdn
```
If origin sends no-cache CDN doesn't serve immutable cached copy. That matches symptom.

jin: service worker trace: fetch handler is checking `event.request.integrity` and falling back to `fetch(event.request, {cache: 'no-store'})` when integrity mismatch. We have a small population where integrity fails (maybe because route served legacy bundle) so SW intentionally bypasses cache.

tess: interesting — there's also a routing-policy tweak last week that prefers dedicated-instance routes but falls back to legacy-route when capacity quota exceeded. Legacy route still serves the old, larger chunk names and doesn't have the same immutable cache headers. So some users flip between variants -> integrity mismatch -> SW network fetch -> repeated downloads.

sam: that explains the correlation with quota spikes. When Dedicated pool is throttled, routing fallback flips a user mid-session. The SW sees a different chunk URL/byte signature and invalidates.

ben: action items proposed: 1) pause canary rollout, 2) make fallback add a header X-Route-Variant so SW can treat as stable (or avoid integrity check failure), 3) make origin set proper `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for chunked assets.

alex: I'm +1 on pausing canary now. We should also avoid sending no-cache from origin — looks like a config change in CDN origin TTL. @infra can we check origin config? :eyes:

jin: quick patch I can push: loosen SW integrity logic to allow same-named chunk if route-variant header differs, so we don't escalate to `no-store` immediately. But that's a bandaid — long term we need consistent cache headers.

jia: agreed. also add telemetry tag for `route_variant_change` so we can count mid-session flips. Right now the telemetry attributes only show final route. Hard to debug without flip count.

sam: I've opened a small dashboard (console -> infra-metrics -> /dash/route-flips) to track flips and chunk re-download counts. Will add alert if >10 flips/min per 1000 users.

tess: one more oddity — a subset of users behind certain CDNs in APAC see 304s instead of 200, but with `pragma: no-cache`. Those still trigger SW validation path. We should sync CDN and origin cache policies globally.

ben: plan:
- immediate: pause frontend canary (ben)
- infra: verify origin TTLs + remove no-cache (alex/@infra)
- sw: push minor relaxation patch to reduce full re-fetchs (jin)
- product/telemetry: add `route_variant_change` event and dashboard (jia/sam)
- follow-up: change fallback to preserve chunk immutability or route users to a compatibility header rather than full legacy asset (tess/ben)

alex: I'll open the CDN ticket and link this thread. If we don't see improvement within 30m after pausing canary, we'll roll back.

jia: thanks — assigning owners in the ticket. tagging @infra and @release for visibility.

deploy-bot: rollback request queued by ben — awaiting approval.

sam: quick note for postmortem: consider adding a canary test that simulates quota-based route fallback to catch cache-variant regressions before rollout. Small N synthetic users that flip routes mid-session.

tess: agreed. Also consider adding a lightweight route-variant header check in the SW that logs, so we can build a fine-grained metric without changing core flow.

jian: (follow-up) initial telemetry shows flips dropping to near-zero 12 minutes after pause. chunk re-downloads down ~85%. Looks like pause helped.

jia: nice — keep monitoring. We'll collect logs and write a short RCA once infra confirms cache headers.

ben: dropping links: CDN ticket -> https://internal.cdn/tickets/6789, SW patch PR -> https://git.internal/redwood/console/pulls/1123

alex: thanks all. :thumbsup:
